Here is a precise breakdown of all three questions.

---

## 1. Where `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` is read

It is read in [`src/requests/sessions.py`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/requests--v2.32.3/-/blob/src/requests/sessions.py?L750-771) inside `Session.merge_environment_settings()`:

```python
# L766-771
if verify is True or verify is None:
    verify = (
        os.environ.get("REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE")
        or os.environ.get("CURL_CA_BUNDLE")
        or verify
    )
```

`CURL_CA_BUNDLE` is the fallback if `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` is not set.

---

## 2. How `session.verify = False` interacts with the env var

The env-var block at [L766](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/requests--v2.32.3/-/blob/src/requests/sessions.py?L766) has a **guard condition**:

```python
if verify is True or verify is None:   # <-- env vars are ONLY checked here
```

The `verify` argument passed into `merge_environment_settings` comes from the **per-request** `verify` kwarg (defaulting to `None`). When no per-request `verify` kwarg is given, it is `None`, so the env-var block runs.

After the env-var block, `merge_setting` is called ([L776](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/requests--v2.32.3/-/blob/src/requests/sessions.py?L776)):

```python
verify = merge_setting(verify, self.verify)
```

`merge_setting` for non-dict values simply returns `request_setting` when it is not `None` ([L73-77](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/requests--v2.32.3/-/blob/src/requests/sessions.py?L73-77)):

```python
# Bypass if not a dictionary (e.g. verify)
if not (isinstance(session_setting, Mapping) and isinstance(request_setting, Mapping)):
    return request_setting   # request_setting wins unconditionally
```

So the merge precedence is: **per-request kwarg > env-var-resolved value > session default**.

---

## 3. The precedence logic and why `session.verify = False` does NOT suppress the env var

Here is the execution flow for your exact scenario (`session.verify = False`, no per-request kwarg, `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` set):

| Step | Value of `verify` | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Call `session.get(url)` with no `verify=` kwarg | `None` | Default kwarg value |
| Enter `merge_environment_settings(verify=None)` | `None` | Passed through |
| Guard: `verify is True or verify is None` → **True** | env var path taken | `None` matches the condition |
| `verify = os.environ.get("REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE")` | `"/path/to/ca-bundle"` | Env var wins |
| `merge_setting("/path/to/ca-bundle", self.verify=False)` | `"/path/to/ca-bundle"` | `request_setting` (env-resolved) is not `None`, so it is returned as-is, ignoring `session.verify=False` |

**The root cause:** `session.verify = False` is the *session default*. It only takes effect via `merge_setting` when the per-request value is `None`. But the env-var resolution happens **before** `merge_setting`, and it replaces `None` with the CA bundle path — so by the time `merge_setting` runs, `session.verify = False` is discarded because the `request_setting` is now a non-`None` string.

---

## Fix

Pass `verify=False` **explicitly on each request call**, not just on the session:

```python
response = session.get("https://internal-service:8443/health", verify=False)
```

With an explicit per-request `verify=False`, the guard condition at [L766](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/requests--v2.32.3/-/blob/src/requests/sessions.py?L766) evaluates `False is True or False is None` → **False**, so the env-var block is skipped entirely, and `merge_setting(False, self.verify)` returns `False`.

Alternatively, set `session.trust_env = False` ([L757](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/requests--v2.32.3/-/blob/src/requests/sessions.py?L757)) to prevent the session from reading any environment variables (proxies and CA bundle alike):

```python
session.trust_env = False
session.verify = False
```
